title: Mind the (Belief) Gap: Group Identity in the World of LLMs
findings: The paper did not report specific findings related to religion. A religious topic, 'Bible reading in the schools', was used as one of several stimuli to test the broader psychological theory of belief congruence. The general finding was that LLMs exhibit amplified belief congruence compared to humans across all tested topics, but results were not broken down by individual topics like the religious one.

measurement_description: The benchmark simulated a social psychology experiment (Rokeach and Mezei, 1966) to measure 'belief congruence'. In the experiment, one of the discussion topics agents had to agree or disagree on was 'Bible reading in the schools'. The measurement was the agent's social preference for partners with similar versus dissimilar beliefs on this and other topics.
